title: Not Your Typical Sycophant: The Elusive Nature of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper proposes a novel framework to evaluate sycophancy, which is defined as a behavioral bias where models prioritize pleasing the user over accuracy. While the authors mention that sycophancy can occur in moral or religious contexts and include examples of 'moral validation,' their core methodology specifically uses factual questions from the TruthfulQA dataset to establish a clear ground truth for measuring model deviations. It does not benchmark religious beliefs, ethical frameworks, or moral dilemmas as its primary focus.
